Proceedings:- Mr. Lea appeared for the Police.
Mr. Wong & Kui for the accused.

Appellant:- I am employed in the Trademark Bureau.
Judge:- Your case was sent back from the Supreme Court
for re-trial.

Mr. Lea:- The Police received three summonses from this
court, but only one was served on this accused, the other two cannot
belocated.

Mr. Wong:- I have a witness of the "Kwang Ming" Newspaper.
Mr. Lea:- The prosecution for the Police is the same as at
the previous trial.

Appellant:- The paper which I gave to the other man to sell is
the Kwang Ming paper. I asked Sue Vung Kwei to sell the paper for
three months. I did not give him any other paper. Sue said that I
had given him other papers, because he was angry, and the reason for
him being angry is because I had asked him to return some money. I
did not give any "Ming Tsing Tsa Suh Ker" newspapers to him.

Witness. Lee Tuh Wei:- I am a pressman and also a teacher in
a school. On the 18th September, 1932, I published the Kwang Ming
newspaper, and the appellant was the editor. The paper ceased its
publication when the trouble started with the Japanese. I reported
to the Bureau of Education when I started to publish the paper. It
is not necessary to report to the Shanghai Municipal Council. The
organisation of the paper was not properly completed, so we did not
give full details to the Bureau of Education. Only my name appeared
on the report. The paper was issued every three days, and I asked
the appellant to give the paper to agents to sell. I do not know
the agents, because I never dealt with them. I know that one of the
agents was named Sue, but I do not know his full name. I do not know
the total number of papers published. I do not know anything about
the Ming Tsing Tsa Suh Ker, nor do I know who ran the paper.

Appellant:- I know the witness. He ran the Kwang Ming news-
paper, but I do not know how much capital he had. I took charge of
the contents of the paper. The paper was printed in the "Hong Keu"

about 3000 papers, and paid/$6.00 every time we printed. I asked
Lue to sell the papers, but Lue never cleared his accounts. If he
sold about 2000 papers, he would only give me the money for 1000.

Among other anti-Government propaganda the 56th issue of the
First Volume of the "Masses" contains an article entitled "Down
with the Reactionary Government and establish a Revolutionary
Political power" of which the following is a summary translation.
--------------------------
The Chief of the Reactionary Ruling Class Chiang Kai-shek since
the establishment of the Nanking Government, carried out his reactionary
policy both in dealing with the internal and foreign affairs of the
country. The Chinese people for maintaining their existence has fought
with the vanguard of the imperialists, Japan, but the Government, on
the contrary, adopts its non-resistance policy and offered one after
the other the Eastern Three Provinces and Shanghai; the Chinese people
for supporting the Northern Eastern Volunteer Armies promoted self
armed organizations, but the Reactionary Government has disbanded them
by force and prevented the people from saving the nation by various
means. Moreover it extorts the sweat money of the toiling masses to
maintain its armies in suppressing its people. Now the time for a new
revolution become mature and every one should exert his effort to
restore the political power from the reactionary rulers to the hands of
the people and materialize the emancipation of the nation.

--------------------------
自南京政府成立以来，反动统治阶级的头子蒋介石在处理国家内政和外交事务上均推行其反动政策。中国人民为维持生存，已与帝国主义先锋日本进行了斗争，但政府反而采取不抵抗政策，将东三省和上海相继拱手相让；中国人民为支持东北义勇军而自发组织武装，但反动政府却以武力解散这些组织，并以各种手段阻止人民救国。此外，它还榨取劳苦大众的血汗钱来维持军队以镇压人民。现在，新革命的时机已经成熟，每个人都应努力将政治权力从反动统治者手中夺回，交还到人民手中，以实现民族的解放。
